title: InterArch: Video Transformer Acceleration via Inter-Feature Deduplication with Cube-based Dataflow
problem: Video Transformer models suffer from substantial computational demands and high energy consumption. Current acceleration methods focus on intra-feature sparsity but neglect inter-feature redundancy and incur prolonged fine-tuning latency.
motivation: Video Transformers show promise for video-oriented tasks, but their computational efficiency must be improved to enable broader deployment.
method: InterArch employs a hierarchical inter-feature deduplication algorithm that exploits temporal similarities at block and element levels to eliminate redundant computations across video frames. A lightweight recovery mechanism constructs approximate features to avoid fine-tuning overhead. A cube-based dataflow consolidates sparse features and translates sparse computations into dense operations. A spatial array architecture with augmented processing elements is optimized to execute this dataflow efficiently.
key_novelty: Hierarchical inter-feature deduplication exploiting temporal redundancy across features, combined with cube-based dataflow that transforms sparse computations into dense operations.
contributions: Inter-feature sparsity algorithm with hierarchical deduplication and lightweight recovery mechanism
Cube-based dataflow strategy consolidating sparse features and converting them to dense computations
Spatial array architecture with augmented processing elements optimized for the proposed dataflow
Demonstrated performance speedups and energy savings on Video Transformer models
